i asked the backend team what need to be done for openfort configuration on the backend side. They came back that nothing is needed on the backend but made same valuable comments what to look out for on the frontend side , like CSP config. Read that (below) and update the file if they mentioned anything missing or worth adding.
---
2. Server-Side Configuration for Google, Apple, Passkey Auth

    Short answer: No server-side code changes are needed on your Go backend. These are all
    client-side (frontend) + Openfort dashboard configurations. Your backend already passes
    INFRA_AUTH_OPENFORT_PUBLISHABLE_KEY and validates JWTs — that's all it needs.

    Here's what's required per provider:

    Auth Method      │ Where to Configure           │ Server-Side Action          
    -----------------+------------------------------+-----------------------------
    **Google OAuth** │ 1. Google Cloud Console →    │ **None** — your backend just
                     │ create OAuth client ID +     │ receives the JWT
                     │ secret 2. Openfort Dashboard │
                     │ → Providers → add Google     │
                     │ credentials + redirect URL   │
    **Apple OAuth**  │ 1. Apple Developer Console → │ **None** — your backend just
                     │ App ID, Services ID, signing │ receives the JWT
                     │ key 2. Openfort Dashboard →  │
                     │ Providers → add Apple        │
                     │ credentials + redirect URL   │
    **Passkey**      │ Frontend `OpenfortProvider`  │ **None** — passkeys are
                     │ config → set                 │ WebAuthn, handled entirely
                     │ `walletRecovery.defaultMetho │ client-side via Openfort SDK
                     │ d:                           │
                     │ RecoveryMethod.PASSKEY`      │

    Important: the feature branch deployment does need one Openfort dashboard change — you must add
     the feature deployment's domain (or IP:port) to the Allowed Origins in your Openfort project's
     security settings, and add the OAuth redirect URL. Without this, the publishable key won't
    work on the feature instance and OAuth callbacks will fail.

      Allowed Origins:  https://beta.infrafund.net, http://<feature-server-ip>:8081
      OAuth Redirect:   https://beta.infrafund.net/auth/callback,
      http://<feature-server-ip>:8081/auth/callback

    Also note from the CSP docs: if your frontend enforces Content-Security-Policy, you'll need
    frame-src https://embed.openfort.io and connect-src https://api.openfort.io 
    https://shield.openfort.io — but this is a frontend concern, not your Go backend.

    CSP headers (if backend serves frontend or sets headers)

    If the Go API sets CSP headers, add these connect-src entries:
    •  https://api.openfort.io
    •  https://embed.openfort.io
    •  https://shield.openfort.io

    And frame-src https://embed.openfort.io for the Openfort embedded wallet iframe.

    ──────────────────────────────────────────

    Summary of work items:
    1. Create deployer-feature.yml workflow
    2. Create docker-compose-feature.yml
    3. Add DOCKER_COMPOSE_PATH_FEATURE GitHub variable
    4. In Openfort Dashboard: add feature instance origin to Allowed Origins + OAuth redirects
    5. In Openfort Dashboard: configure Google + Apple providers (credentials + redirect URLs)
    6. Frontend: add AuthProvider.GOOGLE, AuthProvider.APPLE to uiConfig.authProviders and set
       RecoveryMethod.PASSKEY
    7. (Optional later) nginx config for openfort.beta.infrafund.net domain

actually , i was thinking about the option that a user , after successful login, can delete his own account

---

does our frontend have a 'user account' page ? if not then that would be a good addition, at at the bottom we would have a button [DELETE MY ACCOUNT]
This is what we are going to implement on the backend now :
```
Add `DELETE /v1/me` endpoint for self-service account deletion

    Summary

    Add an authenticated endpoint that allows a logged-in user to
    delete their own account. Uses the existing soft-delete pattern
    (deleted_at) already present in the User entity.

    Architecture (existing DDD layers)

      Handler → AuthService → (UserRepo + SessionRepo + Openfort)

    Changes by layer

    1. SQL — 
    `internal/infrastructure/persistence/postgres/queries/user.sql`

    Add two queries:
    •  SoftDeleteUser — sets deleted_at = NOW(), 
       data_deletion_requested_at = NOW() by user ID
    •  DeleteUserOrganization — deletes from user_organizations by user
        ID

    Then re-run sqlc generate.

    2. Repository — `internal/domain/user/repository/user.go`

    Add method to UserRepo interface:
    •  SoftDelete(ctx, userID uuid.UUID) error

    3. Postgres repo — 
    `internal/infrastructure/persistence/postgres/user_repo.go`

    Implement SoftDelete using the new sqlc query + org cleanup,
    wrapped in a transaction.

    4. Openfort client — `internal/infrastructure/external/openfort/`

    Add a DeleteUser(ctx, openfortUserID string) error method that
    calls the Openfort backend API (DELETE /iam/v1/users/{id}) with the
     secret key. The Openfort JS SDK has deleteUserProject confirming
    this API exists.

    5. Auth service interface — `internal/domain/auth/service/auth.go`

    Add method:
    •  DeleteAccount(ctx, userID uuid.UUID) error

    6. Auth service impl — `internal/application/auth/auth.go`

    Implement DeleteAccount:
    1. Fetch user by ID
    2. Revoke all sessions (sessRepo.RevokeAllByUserID)
    3. Soft-delete user + organization (userRepo.SoftDelete)
    4. Call openfort.DeleteUser to remove Openfort-side identity
    5. Steps 2-3 in a DB transaction; step 4 best-effort (log warning
       on failure, don't block)

    7. Handler — `internal/interfaces/rest/handler/auth.go`

    Add DeleteAccount handler method — reads userID from auth context,
    calls svc.DeleteAccount, returns success + clears refresh cookie.

    8. Input/Output — `internal/interfaces/rest/input/auth.go` + 
    `output/auth.go`
    •  Input: reuse CurrentUserInput (no body needed)
    •  Output: reuse LogoutOutput (success body + clear cookie)

    9. Router — `internal/interfaces/rest/router/auth.go`

    Register new route:

    go
      huma.Register(r.v1, huma.Operation{
          OperationID: "DeleteAccount",
          Summary:     "Delete account",
          Description: "Soft-delete the current user's account and 
      revoke all sessions",
          Method:      fiber.MethodDelete,
          Path:        "/me",
          Tags:        []string{"Auth"},
          Errors:      []int{500, 401},
          Middlewares: huma.Middlewares{r.auth.Auth()},
      }, ah.DeleteAccount)

    Flow diagram

    mermaid
      sequenceDiagram
          participant FE as Frontend
          participant API as DELETE /v1/me
          participant Auth as AuthService
          participant DB as Postgres
          participant OF as Openfort API

          FE->>API: DELETE /v1/me (Bearer token)
          API->>Auth: DeleteAccount(userID)
          Auth->>DB: RevokeAllSessions(userID)
          Auth->>DB: SoftDeleteUser(userID)
          Auth->>DB: DeleteUserOrganization(userID)
          Auth->>OF: DeleteUser(openfortUserID)
          OF-->>Auth: OK (best-effort)
          Auth-->>API: success
          API-->>FE: 200 + Set-Cookie clear

    Frontend (`../front-pro`)

    No backend changes needed on the frontend — just call DELETE /v1/me
     with the access token, then call openfort.auth.signOut() on the
    Openfort SDK side to clear the client-side session state.

    Notes
    •  Soft-delete preserves audit trail; the
       data_deletion_scheduled_at field can be used later for a GDPR
       purge cron job
    •  Openfort deletion is best-effort — if it fails we log but don't
       roll back the local deletion (the user can no longer log in
       anyway)
    •  Existing deleted_at IS NULL filters in all read queries already
       exclude soft-deleted users
```

---

message from backend :
Implemented DELETE /v1/me: it revokes all sessions, soft-deletes the 
   local user, clears the refresh cookie, and frees the deleted user’s 
   email/phone/Openfort ID so the same person can go through the 
   new-user path again.  
   If INFRA_AUTH_OPENFORT_SECRET_KEY is set, the backend also 
   best-effort deletes the Openfort user via DELETE /v2/users/{id}; on 
   the frontend, call this endpoint after login and then 
   openfort.auth.signOut() to clear client state.  
   Verified with make sqlc, make mock, make fmt, make test-unit, make 
   vet, make lint, and make build.
